historical_reviews.deepseek: Directionally aligned on the selector, but cannot validate any referential relationship from a heading filter and its access method is unsuitable for protected evidence.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains the right classification and general linkage intent; its field contract is corrected to the exact Type 35 description and three handle references.

historical_reviews.v3_1: DMTF Type 35 associates a Type 34 management device with a probe/cooling component and optionally a Type 36 threshold record; correctness is referential integrity, not an address or status field.

original_test_intent: Verify every SMBIOS Type 35 Management Device Component structure and its exact association among a Type 34 management device, a managed probe/cooling component and optional Type 36 threshold data against the approved platform topology.
original_method: Preserve existing evidence, collect complete raw Type 35 plus referenced Type 34/component/Type 36 handles through protected read-only access, decode descriptions and handle fields, and prove every non-sentinel link resolves to the expected structure without changing management state.
manual_activity: The platform/BMC owner supplies the expected Type 35 description and handle topology, including allowed FFFFh threshold sentinel; an operator verifies target identity and protected access while automation validates links.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/board, BIOS, SMBIOS and management-controller identity
Expected Management Device Handle resolving to Type 34
Expected Component Handle resolving to the correct probe or cooling-device structure
Expected Threshold Handle resolving to Type 36 or approved no-threshold sentinel
Supported parser, handle-topology map, redaction and protected evidence policy
safety_requirements: Keep collection read-only; do not probe or configure the referenced devices
Do not change BMC, sensor, threshold, fan or power settings
Do not clear dmesg, syslog or SEL before preserving relevant evidence
Never put passwords on the command line or disable host-key verification
Capture complete Type 35 and referenced structures, not a heading filter
Reject dangling, wrong-type, self-referential or duplicate-unexpected handle relationships
Do not require or fabricate address/status fields absent from Type 35
agent_execution_scope: Validate target and expected Type 35 topology
Collect complete raw `dmidecode --type 35` plus referenced Type 34, component and Type 36 structures through protected access
Parse description and all three handle references exactly
Resolve every handle by type and expected identity, honoring only the documented threshold sentinel
Report missing, dangling, wrong-type and duplicate relationships
Produce no device access, configuration change or verdict
engineer_actions: Approve the management-device/component/threshold topology and allowed sentinel state
Resolve OEM, absent or duplicate associations
Review linkage evidence and own PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The Type 35 selector matches the source, but grep hides all link fields and sshpass/disabled host checking weakens security and target identity; source log clearing is rejected.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Through protected access collect unfiltered Type 35 and all referenced structures, then validate Description, Management Device Handle, Component Handle and Threshold Handle per the official schema; do not access devices or clear logs.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Type 35 scope, SPEC comparison, private script and 10/10-minute estimates remain; evidence-clearing boilerplate is not executed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a directed association graph from each Type 35 record to its Type 34 controller, probe/cooling component and optional Type 36 thresholds, verifying target type, existence and owner-approved cardinality for every edge.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds schema-accurate link validation, referenced-structure collection and evidence preservation while removing GPT V2's nonstandard address/status fields.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A structure heading or isolated Type 35 decode cannot prove that the referenced controller, component and threshold records exist or are the intended types.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: SMBIOS associations describe firmware topology; they do not prove the live sensor/control path is functional, and exercising that path requires separate authorization.

project_override_considerations: A Project may accept FFFFh as no threshold only where the specification allows and the topology matrix expects it. Live BMC sensor inventory is supplemental and cannot replace exact SMBIOS handle integrity.
expected_evidence: Redacted SUT/BIOS/SMBIOS/BMC identity, timestamp and approved Type 35 topology
Complete raw Type 35 plus referenced Type 34/component/Type 36 output and exit status
Parsed descriptions and all management-device/component/threshold handles with raw values
Per-edge existence, target-type, identity, cardinality and sentinel validation
Engineer-owned PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently target Type 35. The address/status expansion appears only in GPT V2 guidance and is corrected by the official DMTF schema without changing Master.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The Type 35 linkage comparison is deterministic once the expected topology, referenced records and sentinel policy are supplied.

review_improvement: Converts a filtered record read into exact cross-handle graph validation and corrects GPT V2's nonstandard address/status fields while protecting management evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: Type 35 carries relationships, not independent sensor values. Each record is only meaningful if its Type 34 controller, probe/cooling component and optional Type 36 thresholds resolve to the right structure types; syntactically valid but dangling or swapped handles are the central failure mode.
